title: lathe
body:
## lathe

Revolves a [radius, height] profile a full turn about the local Z axis to create a surface of revolution (vessels, nozzles, knobs), with optional flat caps at the first and last profile points. Schemaxis generates the quad mesh itself from the profile and segments, then applies the material, centre and smoothShading. Choose it when the shape is axisymmetric; use cylinder or cone for constant or linearly tapering sections.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Radii must be positive and heights must strictly increase; violations fail with INVALID_PROFILE at the profile's authored location during planning whenever the values are known host-side (literals, axes, times, expressions), and again when Blender builds the mesh; profiles that read native observations are checked only when Blender runs.
- The adaptor's recorded native qualification cases cover only a material on a cube; this operation relies on repository examples, not on a recorded qualification case.

Native binding: `lathe`. Output kind: `["data"]`.

| Input port | Multiplicity | Required | Kind |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `material` | one node | yes | `material` |

| Option | Meaning | Type / constraints | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `profile` | Half-section of the shape as [radius, height] pairs, listed from bottom to top: radius is the distance from the local Z axis and height the position along it. The surface passes through every pair, revolved a full turn. Radii must be positive and heights strictly increasing; 2 to 128 pairs. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number","minimum":-100000,"maximum":100000},"minItems":2,"maxItems":2},"minItems":2,"maxItems":128}` | **required** |
| `segments` | Number of angular steps around the axis; each profile point becomes a ring of this many vertices. More segments give a rounder surface. | `{"type":"integer","minimum":3,"maximum":256}` | `64` |
| `caps` | When true the bottom and top rings are closed with flat n-gon faces, making a closed solid; when false both ends stay open like a sleeve. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `true` |
| `centre` | World position [x, y, z] of the point on the revolution axis at profile height 0. Schemaxis assigns it as the object's location, so the mesh itself stays about the local origin and later modifiers that work about that origin (mirror, bend, twist) use this point. The profile heights are measured upwards (+Z) from this point. | `{"type":"array","items":{"type":"number"},"minItems":3,"maxItems":3}` | `[0,0,0]` |
| `smoothShading` | When true, every face of the generated lathe is marked smooth so Blender interpolates normals and the tessellated surface renders without visible facets; when false the faces render flat. Geometry and vertex positions are identical either way. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `false` |
